title: The Turning Point
content:
The afternoon passed peacefully.

After lunch, the three of them settled comfortably in the living room. Yashwanth switched on Netflix, and together they began watching a web series. Laughter echoed through the house as they commented on different scenes, completely losing track of time.

Nearly three hours slipped by.

Siddu stretched his arms and rubbed his eyes.

"Guys," he said with a yawn, "you both continue watching. I'm feeling a little sleepy. I'll take a nap."

"Okay," Sneha and Yashwanth replied together.

Siddu smiled faintly before walking into the bedroom. Within minutes, exhaustion took over, and he fell asleep.

The web series continued for another ten minutes.

Then Yashwanth lowered the volume and turned toward Sneha.

"Sneha... can I ask you something?"

She looked at him curiously.

"Of course."

Yashwanth hesitated for a moment before asking,

"Do you have feelings for Siddu?"

The question caught Sneha completely off guard.

She didn't know how to answer.

Her mind immediately whispered,

"No... he's just a friend."

But her heart refused to agree.

Memories of the train journey, the countless thoughts she had about him, and the happiness she felt whenever he smiled flashed before her eyes.

She remained silent.

Yashwanth noticed the confusion on her face and smiled gently.

"It's alright. You don't have to answer now. I think you're still trying to understand your own feelings."

Sneha lowered her head with a shy smile.

After a brief silence, she looked back at him.

"Can I ask you something?"

"Sure."

"Are Siddu and Shreya... still together?"

Yashwanth looked surprised.

"Wait... he hasn't told you the entire story yet?"

Sneha shook her head.

"No. He's still telling it."

"Where did he stop?"

"He stopped after the principal warned him not to talk to Shreya."

Yashwanth leaned back on the sofa.

A faint smile appeared on his face.

"Then you've only heard the beginning."

Sneha looked at him curiously.

"What do you mean?"

Yashwanth's expression slowly turned serious.

"The real story..."

He paused for a moment.

"...the story that completely changed Siddu's life and made him the person he is today..."

"...begins after that."

Sneha's eyes widened.

"Changed him?"

Yashwanth nodded slowly.

"Yes."

Before Sneha could ask another question, Yashwanth suddenly stood up.

He walked into the bedroom where Siddu was sleeping.

Without any warning...

"SIDDU!"

Siddu jumped up in fright.

"W-What happened?" he asked, looking around in panic.

Sneha couldn't stop herself from laughing.

Yashwanth burst into laughter as well.

"Relax," he said, patting Siddu's shoulder. "Nothing happened."

Siddu sighed in relief.

"You idiot..."

Yashwanth grinned.

"Go freshen up. I'm taking both of you somewhere."

"Where?"

"It's a surprise."

Curious about what Yashwanth had planned, Siddu freshened up. A few minutes later, the three of them booked a cab and began their journey.

The vehicle slowly climbed through the winding mountain roads, passing endless pine forests and breathtaking valleys.

Nearly an hour later, the cab finally came to a stop.

Yashwanth stepped out first.

A cool breeze welcomed them as Sneha and Siddu followed him.

They looked around in amazement.

The place was calm, surrounded by towering pine trees and rolling green hills. Unlike the crowded tourist spots, this place was peaceful, almost untouched.

Yashwanth spread his arms with a smile.

"Welcome..."

He looked at both of them before finishing.

"...to Dagshai."

"A beautiful and peaceful hill town," Yashwanth said with a smile. "Not many people visit this place... and that's exactly what makes it special."
